thought.text: The lockfile references @sw-code 396 times. Let me see what those actually resolve to:

reasoning_content:
Interesting! The lockfile has 396 references to `@sw-code`, but `@sw-code/urbo-ui` is `workspace:*` (an in-repo package). Let me check what the actual non-workspace `@sw-code` packages are in the lockfile, and whether they're really being fetched from npm.pkg.github.com.

Also important: there's no `//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN}` in `.npmrc`! So how is pnpm authenticating against npm.pkg.github.com? GitHub Packages' npm registry requires authentication even for public packages. Without a token, requests to npm.pkg.github.com would fail with 401... unless the package is public and no auth is needed? No — GitHub's npm registry requires auth for all operations, even for public packages.

Wait, let me look at what the actual @sw-code entries in the lockfile are. Let me grep for the resolution lines.

action.command: grep -n "npm.pkg.github.com" /workspace/app/pnpm-lock.yaml | head -8; echo "=== @sw-code resolution lines ==="; grep -nE "^\s+'?@sw-code/[^']+':" /workspace/app/pnpm-lock.yaml | head -10; echo "=== sample context ==="; grep -n -A3 "@sw-code/urbo" /workspace/app/pnpm-lock.yaml | head -30
